## 0. Conventions, imported inputs, and what is proved here

Throughout k is a field of characteristic zero. In Part I we work over an algebraically closed extension; `C` is a smooth projective connected curve of genus `g=6`, and `gamma : C -> P^1` is finite flat of degree 4. All linear systems are complete unless stated.

**Imported inputs, with their exact status.**

- **(H-CE)** The degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl package is taken as a *hypothesis* of the theorem, in exactly the form used by the verified dependency: `gamma_*O_C = O + E^vee` with `E` locally free of rank 3, `X := P(E^vee)` with `p_*O_X(1) = E`, `i : C -> X` a closed immersion with `gamma = p o i`, and the ideal resolution

  `(0.1)   0 -> O_X(-4) tensor p^*det F -> O_X(-2) tensor p^*F -> I_C -> 0`

  for a rank-two `F` on `P^1`. This is satisfied by every finite flat degree-four Gorenstein cover by the Casnati-Ekedahl structure theorem [SRC-0004]; it is stated as a hypothesis rather than imported as a theorem, exactly as ATT-0065 does. From SRC-0004 itself I use only the sign convention `W_f := (O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-f))|_C` (the minus sign is forced; see the recorded convention constraint) and, as a cross-check only, `deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12-4f`. Every degree used below is **re-derived** in Section 1.

- **(H-ATT0065)** The verified dependency artifact **ATT-0065** (subproblem C66-GEO-Z), confirmed by **REV-0108** and **REV-0109** (both verdict `confirmed`, all of CLM-0065-1..9 confirmed). I use only its *intrinsic* clauses: **CLM-0065-1** (`pi_*W`, `pi_*(W|Gamma)` locally free with base change, `Fit_0(coker phi) = I_{2n}(phi)`), **CLM-0065-3** (filtered reduction `coker(phi) = coker(phi_5)`, no global splitting), **CLM-0065-4** (`Fit_0(coker phi) = a_N^* I_e`, hence the intrinsic failure scheme is `a_N^{-1}(e(B))`, stable under arbitrary locally Noetherian base change, descending along smooth atlases) and **CLM-0065-5** (canonical filtration from fibrewise balanced `F`, degrees 20 and 16). I deliberately do **not** invoke the *ambient* comparison clause, because REV-0108's finding candidate FC-AMBIENT-EQN-BUNDLE-REMAINS-HYP records that balancedness does not discharge the separate hypothesis that `q_*script-W` is finite locally free with base change; nothing below needs it.

**What is genuinely new here** is Section 2 (the monomial obstruction `f_1 <= 2 e_1`) and its consequences in Sections 3-5, together with the family-level Sections 6-8. ATT-0065's own `theorem_scope.not_covered` lists precisely `h^0` strata, nonemptiness of the reduced-support open, dimensions and components; those are the deliverables of C66-COMP-RANK and are what is proved below.

**No finite computation is load-bearing.** The only explicit example (Section 9) is used solely to prove a nonemptiness/existence statement, which is not a universal claim.

---

## 1. Numerical normalization of the CE data

Write `E = O(e_1)+O(e_2)+O(e_3)` with `e_1<=e_2<=e_3`, and `F = O(f_1)+O(f_2)` with `f_1<=f_2`.

**(1a) `deg E = 9`.** Since `gamma` is finite, `chi(O_C) = chi(gamma_*O_C) = chi(O_{P^1}) + chi(E^vee) = 1 + (-deg E + 3)`. With `chi(O_C) = 1-g = -5` this gives `deg E = 9`.

**(1b) `p_*O_X(m) = Sym^m E`, and the standard `P^2`-bundle vanishings.** For `X = Proj(Sym E) -> P^1` a `P^2`-bundle with `p_*O_X(1) = E`: `R^i p_* O_X(m) = 0` for all `i` when `m = -1,-2`; `R^{>0}p_*O_X(m)=0` and `p_*O_X(m) = Sym^m E` for `m >= 0`; and `omega_{X/P^1} = O_X(-3) tensor p^*det E`, so relative duality gives `R^2 p_* O_X(-3) = (p_*(O_X(3) tensor omega_{X/P^1}))^vee = (p_* p^* det E)^vee = (det E)^vee`.

**(1c) `deg(O_X(1)|_C) = sum f_i + 9`.** Twist (0.1) by `O_X(1)`:

`0 -> O_X(-3) tensor p^*det F -> O_X(-1) tensor p^*F -> I_C(1) -> 0`,

and `0 -> I_C(1) -> O_X(1) -> O_X(1)|_C -> 0`. All `R^i p_*` of `O_X(-1) tensor p^*F` vanish by (1b), so `R^i p_* I_C(1) = R^{i+1} p_*(O_X(-3) tensor p^*det F)`; hence `p_* I_C(1) = 0` and `R^1 p_* I_C(1) = (det E)^vee tensor det F`. The second sequence then gives

`(1.1)   0 -> E -> gamma_*(O_X(1)|_C) -> (det E)^vee tensor det F -> 0`,

a rank-four sheaf of degree `deg E + deg F - deg E = sum f_i`. For any line bundle `M` on `C`, `chi(M) = chi(gamma_*M) = deg(gamma_*M) + 4`, while `chi(M) = deg M - 5`; hence `deg M = deg(gamma_*M) + 9`. Applying this to `M = O_X(1)|_C` gives `deg(O_X(1)|_C) = sum f_i + 9`.

**(1d) `sum f_i = 9`, `deg(O_X(1)|_C)=18`, and `O_X(1)|_C = omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2)`.** By (0.1) the normal bundle is `N_{C/X} = (O_X(2) tensor p^*O(-f_1))|_C + (O_X(2) tensor p^*O(-f_2))|_C`, so `det N = O_X(4) tensor p^*O(-sum f_i)|_C`. Also `omega_X = omega_{X/P^1} tensor p^*omega_{P^1} = O_X(-3) tensor p^*(det E tensor O(-2))`. Adjunction gives

`(1.2)   omega_C = O_X(1)|_C tensor gamma^*O(deg E - 2 - sum f_i)`.

Taking degrees and using (1c), `deg E = 9` and `deg gamma^*O(1) = 4`:
`10 = (sum f_i + 9) + 4(9 - 2 - sum f_i) = 1 + 36 - 3 sum f_i`, hence `sum f_i = 9`. Then `deg(O_X(1)|_C) = 18` and (1.2) reads `omega_C = O_X(1)|_C tensor gamma^*O(-2)`, i.e.

`(1.3)   O_X(1)|_C = omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2)`.

This reproves, independently of any normalization citation, the relation recorded in the packet as pinning GAP-Z-W5D (FND-0105), and is consistent with SRC-0004's `deg(O_X(2)|_C) = 2(2g-2+8) = 36`.

**(1e) Consequences.** With `D := gamma^*O(1)` of degree 4, (1.3) gives, for any `f`,

`(1.4)   W_f := (O_X(2) tensor p^*O(-f))|_C = omega_C^2 tensor gamma^*O(4-f)`,

so `W_4 = omega_C^2` (degree 20) and `W_5 = omega_C^2(-D)` (degree 16), matching `4g+12-4f`; and

`(1.5)   L := W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} = omega_C(-D)`, of degree `10-4 = 6`.

---

## 2. The monomial obstruction: `f_1 <= 2 e_1`

This is the new step.

**Lemma 2.1.** Under (H-CE), `f_1 <= 2 e_1`.

*Proof.* Dualizing the map `O_X(-2) tensor p^*F -> O_X` of (0.1), the ideal `I_C` is generated by a pair of sections

`q_i in Hom(O_X(-2) tensor p^*O(f_i), O_X) = H^0(X, O_X(2) tensor p^*O(-f_i)) = H^0(P^1, Sym^2 E tensor O(-f_i))`,

and `C = V(q_1,q_2)` scheme-theoretically, since the image of that map is exactly `I_C`.

Let `x_1,x_2,x_3` be the tautological "coordinates" corresponding to the summands `O(e_j) subset E = p_*O_X(1)`; concretely `x_j in H^0(X, O_X(1) tensor p^*O(-e_j))`. Then `Sym^2 E tensor O(-f) = sum_{j<=l} O(e_j+e_l-f)`, with the summand indexed by `(j,l)` being the coefficient of the monomial `x_j x_l`. Hence

`(2.1)   the coefficient of x_1^2 in q_i lies in H^0(P^1, O(2e_1 - f_i)), which is 0 whenever 2e_1 < f_i.`

Suppose, for contradiction, that `2e_1 < f_1 <= f_2`. Then by (2.1) both `q_1` and `q_2` have vanishing `x_1^2`-coefficient. Let `sigma := V(x_2,x_3) subset X`. Points of `X = Proj(Sym E)` over `t in P^1` are the one-dimensional quotients of `E_t`, and `V(x_2,x_3)` is the locus of quotients killing the subbundle `O(e_2)+O(e_3)`, i.e. the single quotient `E ->> O(e_1)`. Thus `sigma` is a section of `p`, in particular `sigma = P^1` and `p|_sigma` is an isomorphism. Restricting a quadric to `sigma` sets `x_2 = x_3 = 0`, leaving only its `x_1^2`-term; since `x_1|_sigma` is nowhere zero (the projection `E ->> O(e_1)` is nonzero on the summand `O(e_1)`), we get `q_i|_sigma = 0` for `i = 1,2`.

Hence `sigma subset V(q_1,q_2) = C`. Both `sigma` and `C` are integral closed subschemes of dimension one, so `sigma` and `C` have the same underlying space; as `C` is reduced, the ideal of `sigma` in `C` is contained in the nilradical of `O_C`, which is zero, so `sigma = C`. But then `4 = deg(gamma) = deg(p|_sigma) = 1`, a contradiction. Therefore `2 e_1 >= f_1`. QED

**Remark 2.2 (sharpness).** The bound is attained: for a hyperelliptic genus-six curve with `gamma = q o h` (`h` the hyperelliptic map, `q` of degree two), `h_*O_C = O + O(-7)` and `q_*O(a) = O(floor(a/2)) + O(ceil(a/2)-1)` give `gamma_*O_C = O + O(-1) + O(-4) + O(-4)`, i.e. `E = O(1)+O(4)+O(4)` and `e_1 = 1`; Lemma 2.1 then forces `f_1 <= 2`, hence `F = O(f_1)+O(9-f_1)` with `f_1 <= 2`, and in particular `F` is very far from balanced.

---

## 3. Balanced implies `e_1 >= 2`, `h^0(D) = 2`, and non-hyperellipticity

**Proposition 3.1.** Assume `(f_1,f_2) = (4,5)`. Then `e_1 >= 2`, and `h^0(C, O_C(D)) = 2`.

*Proof.* Lemma 2.1 gives `2e_1 >= f_1 = 4`, i.e. `e_1 >= 2`, hence `e_j >= 2` for all `j`. By the projection formula,

`h^0(C, gamma^*O(1)) = h^0(P^1, O(1) tensor gamma_*O_C) = h^0(O(1)) + h^0(E^vee(1)) = 2 + sum_j h^0(O(1-e_j)) = 2 + 0 = 2.` QED

**Proposition 3.2.** If `h^0(C,O_C(D)) = 2` then `gamma` does not factor through a degree-two morphism `C -> P^1`, and `C` is not hyperelliptic.

*Proof.* Suppose `C` is hyperelliptic with hyperelliptic map `h : C -> P^1` of degree 2. Consider `(h,gamma) : C -> P^1 x P^1`, and let `Y` be its image, of class `O(a,b)` with `deg(pr_1|_Y) = b` and `deg(pr_2|_Y) = a`. If `(h,gamma)` were birational onto `Y`, then `(a,b) = (4,2)` and `6 = g(C) <= p_a(Y) = (a-1)(b-1) = 3`, absurd. So `(h,gamma)` has degree `m >= 2` onto `Y`; both `h` and `gamma` then factor through the normalization `Y'` of `Y`, and `2 = deg(h) = m * deg(Y' -> P^1_{first})` forces `m = 2` and `Y' -> P^1_{first}` of degree one, i.e. `Y' = P^1` and `C -> Y'` is `h`. Hence `gamma = q o h` with `deg q = 2`, so `D = h^*(q^*(pt))` is linearly equivalent to `2H` where `H` is the hyperelliptic class, and `h^0(O_C(D)) = h^0(2H) = 3 != 2`, a contradiction. The same computation shows `gamma` cannot factor through any degree-two map to `P^1`, since such a factorization makes `C` hyperelliptic. QED

**Corollary 3.3.** On the balanced locus `F = O(4)+O(5)` there is no tetragonal pencil factoring through a degree-two map; equivalently, **no non-primitive degree-four pencil has balanced CE splitting**. This settles the question that FND-0104 explicitly leaves open and does not assert ("whether a non-primitive degree-4 pencil can have balanced CE splitting F = O(4)+O(5)"), and proves the archive candidate recorded as "h^0(omega_C(-D)) = 3 constantly on the whole balanced tetragonal locus; equivalently ... no non-primitive degree-4 pencil has balanced splitting O(4)+O(5)".

**Remark 3.4 (constraint discipline).** The recorded constraint forbidding the identification of constancy of `h^0(omega_C(-D)) = 3` with the exclusion of *all* non-primitive degree-four pencils is respected: only the hyperelliptic-composite case is excluded, and it is excluded by proof. Degree-four covers factoring through an intermediate curve of genus 1, 2 or 3 are **not** excluded here, and need not be: they satisfy `h^0(O_C(D)) = 2` and are perfectly compatible with everything below.

---

## 4. The residual net `L`, and recovery of the pencil

**Proposition 4.1.** In the balanced case, `L = omega_C(-D)` has `deg L = 6`, `h^0(L) = 3` and `h^1(L) = 2`, exactly.

*Proof.* `deg L = 6` is (1.5). Serre duality gives `h^1(L) = h^0(omega_C tensor L^{-1}) = h^0(O_C(D)) = 2` by Proposition 3.1, and Riemann-Roch gives `h^0(L) = deg L - g + 1 + h^1(L) = 6-6+1+2 = 3`. QED

This is consistent with, and sharpens, the recorded facts `h^0(L) = 1 + h^0(M)` with `M := omega_C^2 tensor W_5^vee` of degree 4 (here `M = O_C(D)` by (1.4)) and the Clifford range `h^0(L) in {1,2,3,4}` with `h^0(L)=4` only on hyperelliptic fibres: the balanced hypothesis pins the value to 3 and excludes the hyperelliptic stratum outright.

**Proposition 4.2 (recovery of `gamma` from `L`).** `omega_C tensor L^{-1} = O_C(D)`, `h^0(O_C(D)) = 2`, and `|O_C(D)|` is base-point-free; hence the morphism defined by `|omega_C tensor L^{-1}|` is `gamma`, up to an automorphism of `P^1`.

*Proof.* `omega_C tensor L^{-1} = omega_C tensor omega_C^{-1}(D) = O_C(D)`. Base-point-freeness: `|D|` contains the pullback `gamma^*|O_{P^1}(1)|`, which is base-point-free because `gamma` is a morphism; since `h^0(O_C(D)) = 2`, `|D|` equals that pullback pencil, and the associated morphism is `gamma`. QED

This is exactly the route which FND-0098 identifies as "the only standard recovery route" for a monomorphism into `M_{6,6}`; it is used in Section 8.

---

## 5. Reduced members of `|L|`

**Lemma 5.1.** Let `C` be a smooth projective connected non-hyperelliptic curve of genus 6 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and `L` a line bundle with `deg L = 6` and `h^0(L) = 3`. Write `|L| = Phi + |M|` with `Phi` the fixed divisor and `|M|` base-point-free, `h^0(M) = 3`. Then:

(i) `deg Phi <= 1`; in particular `Bs|L|` is empty or a single reduced point.

(ii) The set of `Gamma in |L| = P^2` whose support consists of six pairwise distinct points is a nonempty dense open subset with proper closed complement.

(iii) If `deg Phi = 1`, then `C` is a smooth plane quintic, `M = O_C(1)`, `Phi = q` and `L = O_C(1)(q)`.

*Proof.* If `h^1(M) = 0` then `h^0(M) = deg M - 5`, so `deg M = 8 > 6 >= deg M`, absurd; hence `M` is special. Clifford gives `2 = h^0(M)-1 <= deg(M)/2`, so `deg M >= 4`. If `deg M = 4` then equality holds in Clifford with `0 < deg M < 2g-2 = 10`, forcing `C` hyperelliptic, excluded. So `deg M in {5,6}` and `deg Phi = 6 - deg M <= 1`, proving (i).

For (ii), let `phi := phi_{|M|} : C -> P^2` be the morphism attached to the base-point-free net `|M|`; its image spans `P^2` since `h^0(M)=3`. In characteristic zero `phi` is generically immersive, so `R := {p in C : d phi_p = 0}` is a proper closed, hence finite, subset. Members of `|M|` are the divisors `phi^*l`, `l` a line. For `p` with `phi(p) in l`, one has `mult_p(phi^*l) >= 2` iff `l` annihilates the image of `d phi_p`; so if `p` is not in `R` this says `l` is the tangent line to `phi` at `p`, and if `p` is in `R` it is automatic. Hence the set of lines `l` with `phi^*l` non-reduced is contained in `tau(C \ R) union (union over p in R of the pencil of lines through phi(p))`, where `tau` is the tangent-line map. The first piece is the image of a morphism from a curve, of dimension at most 1; the second is a finite union of lines in the dual plane, of dimension 1. So the bad locus is a constructible subset of dimension at most 1 in the two-dimensional dual plane, and for `l` outside a proper closed subset `phi^*l` consists of `deg M` distinct points.

If `Phi = 0` this proves (ii). If `Phi = q` is a single reduced point, then `q` is not a base point of `|M|`, so `h^0(M-q) = 2 < 3` and the members of `|M|` through `q` form a proper linear subspace of `|M| = P^2`; hence for general `l` we have `q` not in `supp(phi^*l)`, and `Phi + phi^*l = q + (5 distinct points, none equal to q)` is reduced of degree 6. Openness of the reduced-support condition is standard (its complement is the image of the proper incidence `{(p,Gamma) : 2p <= Gamma}`), so the reduced locus is open dense in the irreducible `|L| = P^2`.

For (iii): `deg M = 5` and `|M|` is a base-point-free `g^2_5`. Writing `5 = deg(phi) * deg(phi(C))` with `deg(phi(C)) >= 2` (the image spans `P^2`) and `5` prime, we get `deg(phi) = 1`, so `phi` is birational onto a plane quintic `Y` with `p_a(Y) = 6`. Then `6 = g(C) = p_a(Y) - sum_p delta_p` forces all `delta_p = 0`, so `Y` is smooth and `C = Y`, `M = O_C(1)`. Finally `L = M(q) = O_C(1)(q)`, and `D ~ omega_C tensor L^{-1} = O_C(2) tensor O_C(-1)(-q) = O_C(1)(-q)`. QED

**Corollary 5.2.** In the balanced case (Propositions 3.1, 3.2, 4.1), every hypothesis of Lemma 5.1 holds for `L = omega_C(-D)`; hence the six-distinct-points locus is dense open and in particular **nonempty** in `|L| = P^2`.

This discharges the frontier obligation "nonemptiness of the reduced-support open (and of the ordered `Conf_6` incidence) on geometric fibres, beyond `chi(L)=1` nonemptiness" (FND-0083), by exactly the mechanism the recorded constraint says is required (base-point-freeness plus a Bertini-type genericity argument in characteristic zero) - and, beyond that, it also covers the case where `|L|` is *not* base-point-free, which by Lemma 5.1(iii) happens only for smooth plane quintics.

---

## 6. Family form: base change, the `P^2`-bundle, and the regular immersion

Now let `B`, `pi : C -> B`, `s : P -> B`, `gamma : C -> P` be as in Part (II), with every geometric fibre balanced. Fix `O_P(1)` of relative degree one, `D := gamma^*O_P(1)`, `L := omega_{C/B}(-D)`.

**Remark 6.1 (the `Pic(B)`-ambiguity).** `O_P(1)` is unique only up to `s^*Pic(B)`, so `D` and `L` are defined only up to a twist by `pi^*` of an invertible sheaf on `B`. Every statement below is invariant under `L -> L tensor pi^*A`: `P(pi_*L)` is unchanged, and the incidence condition "`O(Gamma) = L` relatively", i.e. "`O(Gamma) tensor L^{-1}` lies in the identity of `Pic^0_{C/B}`", is unchanged. This is the ambiguity flagged by the recorded constraint forbidding quantification of `W_5` or `L` over the whole family rather than over geometric fibres; it is handled, not ignored. No global splitting of `F` or of `W` is used anywhere: fibrewise splitting is used only on geometric fibres, and at family level ATT-0065's canonical *filtration* (CLM-0065-5) is what is invoked.

**Proposition 6.2 (base change, no reducedness needed).** `pi_*L` is locally free of rank 3 and `R^1pi_*L` is locally free of rank 2, and both commute with arbitrary base change `B' -> B`.

*Proof.* By Proposition 4.1 applied to each geometric fibre, `h^0(L_b) = 3` and `h^1(L_b) = 2` for **every** geometric point `b`. Since `pi` is proper flat and `L` is `B`-flat, `R pi_* L` is computed universally by a two-term complex `K^0 -> K^1` of finite locally free sheaves. `R^1 pi_* L = coker(K^0 -> K^1)` commutes with arbitrary base change (right exactness of tensor), and its fibres have constant dimension 2, so it is locally free of rank 2; hence `K^0 -> K^1` has locally constant rank, its image is a subbundle, and `pi_*L = ker(K^0 -> K^1)` is a subbundle of `K^0` whose formation commutes with base change, locally free of rank 3. QED

This is the cohomology-and-base-change argument valid for **non-reduced** locally Noetherian bases requested as an open obligation in the working context, and it is exactly the qualification that the recorded constraint on `Proj(pi_*L)` demands when `h^0(L)` might jump. Here `h^0` does not jump: by Proposition 3.1 the balanced locus is a single `h^0`-stratum.

**Proposition 6.3 (the Abel-Jacobi fibre is a `P^2`-bundle).** Let `AJ := Sym^6(C/B) x_{Pic^6_{C/B},[L]} B` be the closed subscheme of `Sym^6(C/B)` representing relative effective degree-six divisors `Gamma` with `O(Gamma) = L` relatively. Then `AJ` is canonically `B`-isomorphic to the projective bundle `P(pi_*L)` of one-dimensional subbundles, hence smooth and projective over `B`, Zariski-locally trivial with fibres `P^2`, of pure relative dimension 2.

*Proof.* Closedness of `AJ` in `Sym^6(C/B)` holds because `Pic^6_{C/B}` is separated (this is the model recorded as FND-0107; on a smooth relative curve `Hilb^6 = Sym^6`). For the identification, compare functors of points on `B`-schemes `T`. A `T`-point of `AJ` is a relative effective Cartier divisor `Gamma subset C_T`, finite flat of degree 6 over `T`, with `O(Gamma) = L_T tensor pi_T^*N` for some invertible `N` on `T` (fppf-locally on `T`; both functors are fppf sheaves, so it suffices to compare after fppf localization). The tautological section `1_Gamma` then becomes a section `sigma` of `L_T tensor pi_T^*N`, i.e. by Proposition 6.2 an element of `Hom_T(N^{-1}, (pi_*L)_T)`, and `sigma_t != 0` for every `t in T` because `Gamma` is a relative divisor; hence `N^{-1} -> (pi_*L)_T` is fibrewise injective, i.e. a subbundle inclusion. Conversely, a subbundle `N^{-1} -> (pi_*L)_T` yields a section of `L_T tensor pi_T^*N` nonzero on every fibre, whose zero scheme is a relative effective Cartier divisor of degree 6 with the required property. The two constructions are mutually inverse, and the residual scaling is precisely what `P(-)` quotients. QED

**Corollary 6.4 (rank-drop fibre dimension and excess).** For every geometric point `b` of `B`, the fibre of `AJ` over `b` is `|L_b| = P^2`, of dimension exactly 2. The closed immersion `AJ -> Sym^6(C/B)` is a regular immersion of codimension 4, both being smooth over `B` (of relative dimensions 2 and 6).

*Proof.* The fibre statement is Proposition 6.3 plus Proposition 4.1. A closed immersion of schemes smooth over a common base is a regular immersion of codimension the difference of the relative dimensions. QED

**Remark 6.5 (expected versus actual codimension: what is and is not concluded).** By the imported CLM-0065-1 and CLM-0065-3 the rank-drop ideal is `Fit_0(coker phi) = I_{12}(phi) = I_6(phi_5)`, the ideal of maximal minors of the corank-at-most-one evaluation `phi_5` of ranks `11 -> 6`; its generic determinantal expectation is codimension `(11-5)(6-5) = 6`, while Corollary 6.4 gives actual codimension 4, the excess being `h^1(L) = 2`. The comparison "expected 6 versus actual 4" is already recorded in the working context and is **not** claimed as new; what is new is that by Propositions 3.1 and 4.1 the excess is now known to be *constant equal to 2 over the whole balanced locus*, not merely on a dominant component. In accordance with the recorded constraint I do **not** infer local complete intersection, smoothness, closedness, Gysin, purity or Tate type *from the excess identity*. Corollary 6.4 does establish, by direct computation rather than by any excess bookkeeping, that the incidence scheme is smooth over `B` and regularly embedded of codimension 4; this answers the recorded "nowhere-lci" guess in the opposite direction, and shows why that inference was correctly blocked.

---

## 7. The reduced-support open, the ordering torsor, and comparison with ATT-0065

**Proposition 7.1.** The reduced-support locus `AJ^{rs} subset AJ` (divisors with six pairwise distinct support points) is open, meets every geometric fibre of `AJ -> B` in a dense open subset, and is therefore dense open in `AJ` with `AJ^{rs} -> B` smooth and surjective with geometrically irreducible two-dimensional fibres.

*Proof.* Openness: the complement is the image of the proper incidence locus, hence closed. Fibrewise density and nonemptiness: Corollary 5.2 applied to each geometric fibre. Smoothness and surjectivity then follow from Proposition 6.3. QED

**Proposition 7.2.** Let `Z := Conf_6(C/B) x_{Sym^6(C/B)} AJ`, where `Conf_6(C/B)` is the open subscheme of the sixfold fibre product parametrizing ordered pairwise-distinct points. Then `Conf_6(C/B) -> Sym^6(C/B)` is a finite etale `S_6`-torsor onto the reduced-support open, so `Z -> AJ^{rs}` is a finite etale `S_6`-torsor; consequently `Z` is smooth over `B` of pure relative dimension 2, and `Z -> B` is surjective.

*Proof.* `S_6` acts freely on ordered pairwise-distinct points, and a free action of a finite group gives an etale torsor onto the quotient, which is the reduced-support open of `Sym^6`; this is the model recorded as FND-0064, stated at stack level on the *open subschemes* with no reduction applied to either side (respecting the recorded constraints that forbid asserting the torsor on coarse moduli and forbid reducing only the source). Base change of a finite etale torsor is a finite etale torsor, and etale morphisms preserve smoothness over `B`. QED

**Proposition 7.3 (identification with the CE evaluation-failure scheme).** Apply ATT-0065 with base `B' := Conf_6(C/B)`, which carries the pulled-back balanced family and the six tautological pairwise-disjoint sections `x_1,...,x_6` with `Gamma = sum x_i(B')`. Then the intrinsic CE evaluation-failure scheme `V(Fit_0(coker phi)) = a_N^{-1}(e(B'))` on `B'` equals `Z`.

*Proof.* The hypotheses of ATT-0065 hold: `n = 6 >= 1` pairwise disjoint sections; by CLM-0065-5 the fibrewise balanced `F` yields the canonical filtration `0 -> W_4 -> W -> W_5 -> 0` with constant fibre degrees `d_4 = 20`, `d_5 = 16`, and `20-6 = 14 > 10 = 2g-2`, `16-6 = 10 = 2g-2`, which are exactly the required degree inequalities. CLM-0065-4 then gives that the failure scheme is `a_N^{-1}(e)` for `N = omega_{C/B'} tensor W_5^vee(Gamma)`.

It remains to see that `a_N` and the Abel-Jacobi map `Gamma -> O(Gamma) tensor L^{-1}` agree as maps to `Pic^0`. Since `L_5 subset F` is a line bundle of relative degree 5 on the `P^1`-bundle `P`, we have `L_5 = O_P(5) tensor s^*A_1` for some invertible `A_1` on `B`, so `W_5 = O_X(2)|_C tensor gamma^*O_P(-5) tensor pi^*A_1^{-1}`. Moreover the line bundle `O_X(1)|_C tensor omega_{C/B}^{-1} tensor gamma^*O_P(-2)` restricts to `O` on every geometric fibre by (1.3), hence equals `pi^*A_2` for some invertible `A_2` on `B` (a line bundle on a smooth proper family with geometrically connected fibres that is fibrewise trivial is a pullback, since `pi_*O_C = O_B`). Therefore `W_5 = omega_{C/B}^2(-D) tensor pi^*A` for an invertible `A` on `B`, so

`N = omega tensor W_5^vee(Gamma) = O(Gamma) tensor omega^{-1}(D) tensor pi^*A^{-1} = O(Gamma) tensor L^{-1} tensor pi^*A^{-1}`,

and `a_N` equals the Abel-Jacobi map, because `Pic^0_{C/B}` identifies line bundles differing by a pullback from the base. Hence `a_N^{-1}(e(B')) = Conf_6(C/B) x_{Sym^6(C/B)} AJ = Z`. QED

**Corollary 7.4 (components and dimensions over the balanced locus).** Over the balanced locus, the CE evaluation-failure scheme `Z` is smooth over `B` of pure relative dimension exactly 2, is a finite etale `S_6`-torsor over a fibrewise-dense open subscheme of a Zariski-locally trivial `P^2`-bundle, and has **no** fibre of dimension different from 2 and **no** component of relative dimension greater than 2 over any point of `B`, however special the curve. In particular no larger component appears over hyperelliptic, plane-quintic, bielliptic, trigonal or any other special locus of `B`: by Proposition 3.2 the hyperelliptic case does not occur in `B` at all, and by Proposition 4.1 there is no jumping of `h^0(L)`.

This is the balanced-locus part of the frontier obligation on components, dimensions and "exclusion of larger components over special curve loci". It is a statement about the model over `B`; the number of `g^1_4`'s on a fibre affects the fibres of `B -> M_6`, not the fibres of `Z -> B`.

---

## 8. Dimension, and the classifying morphism

**Proposition 8.1.** If `B` is of finite type over `k` of pure dimension `b`, then `Z` is of pure dimension `b+2` and every irreducible component of `Z` dominates a component of `B`.

*Proof.* `Z -> B` is smooth surjective of pure relative dimension 2 (Propositions 7.1, 7.2), and `AJ = P(pi_*L)` is a Zariski-locally trivial `P^2`-bundle, so over each component of `B` the corresponding part of `AJ` is irreducible of dimension `(dim of that component) + 2`, and `Z` is finite etale over a dense open of it. QED

**Proposition 8.2 (monomorphism).** Assume in addition that `B` is a moduli stack of balanced tetragonal covers: its `T`-points are pairs `(C/T, gamma : C -> P)` as above and its isomorphisms are the isomorphisms of such pairs. Then the classifying morphism `c : Z -> M_{6,6}`, `(b; p_1,...,p_6) -> (C_b; p_1,...,p_6)`, is a monomorphism of stacks: fully faithful on `T`-points, in particular injective on isomorphism classes of geometric points and inducing isomorphisms on automorphism groups.

*Proof.* First, `c` is well defined: a point of `Z` is a fibre `C_b` (smooth, genus 6) together with six **pairwise distinct** ordered points, which is exactly a point of `M_{6,6}`; this is where the reduced-support condition of Proposition 7.1 is indispensable.

Let `z, z'` be `T`-points of `Z`, given by `(C/T, gamma, x_1..x_6)` and `(C'/T, gamma', x'_1..x'_6)`, and let `psi : C -> C'` be an isomorphism over `T` with `psi(x_i) = x'_i`, i.e. an isomorphism `c(z) -> c(z')`. Then `psi^*O(Gamma') = O(Gamma)`; since `Gamma` and `Gamma'` are points of the respective incidences, `O(Gamma) = L tensor pi^*(\cdot)` and `O(Gamma') = L' tensor pi'^*(\cdot)`, so `psi^*L' = L tensor pi^*(\cdot)`, hence

`psi^*(omega_{C'/T} tensor L'^{-1}) = omega_{C/T} tensor L^{-1} tensor pi^*(\cdot)`, i.e. `psi^*O(D') = O(D) tensor pi^*(\cdot)`.

By Proposition 4.2 applied fibrewise, `h^0(O(D_t)) = 2` and `h^1(O(D_t)) = 3` are constant, so `pi_*O(D)` is locally free of rank two with base change (same argument as Proposition 6.2), the relative pencil `|D|` is relatively base-point-free, and the morphism it defines is `gamma` followed by the canonical identification of `P` with the `P^1`-bundle `P(pi_*O(D))`. The displayed isomorphism therefore induces an isomorphism `theta : P -> P'` with `gamma' o psi = theta o gamma`, i.e. `(psi,theta)` is an isomorphism `b -> b'` in `B` carrying `x_i` to `x'_i`; that is an isomorphism `z -> z'` in `Z` mapping to `psi`. It is unique, since an isomorphism of `Z`-objects is determined by its underlying `psi` (`theta` is determined by `psi` because `gamma` is surjective). Hence `c` is fully faithful. QED

**Corollary 8.3 (image dimension).** Under the hypotheses of Propositions 8.1 and 8.2, `c` has zero-dimensional geometric fibres, so the image of `c` has dimension `b+2`. For `b = 15` this is `17 = 21 - 4`, i.e. codimension 4 in `M_{6,6}`.

**Remark 8.4 (which blocked inference this is, and why it is now licensed).** The working context blocks concluding, from "`AJ_B = P(p_*L_B)` of pure relative dimension 2" together with "geometric-point injectivity of the classifying map", that the image of the reduced-support open has dimension `dim B + 2` - for the stated reason that the reduced-support locus is only an *open* subset of the `P^2`-bundle and could be fibrewise empty. Corollary 5.2 and Proposition 7.1 supply exactly that missing input (fibrewise nonemptiness, indeed density), and Proposition 8.2 supplies the injectivity by proof rather than by assumption. The inference of Corollary 8.3 is therefore not the blocked one: it does not rest on the two inputs alone. Correspondingly, the recorded constraint that a source-dimension count `15+2 = 17` does not by itself determine image dimension, fibre dimension, component purity, stabilizers or closure behaviour is respected: the fibre dimension is computed (Corollary 6.4), the generic fibre of `c` is controlled (Proposition 8.2), and **no** claim of purity, closedness, or component structure of the failure locus inside `M_{6,6}` is made. The value `b = 15` is an *input*, not proved here; it presupposes simple branching (the recorded constraint on `b = 2g-2+2d` as a branch-point count) and the identification of `B` with the balanced open of the Hurwitz stack, and the passage between coarse-space and stack dimension recorded in FND-0060 is not carried out.

---

## 9. The balanced locus is nonempty (so the theorem is not vacuous)

Let `X_0 = P^1 x P^2` and let `C` be the intersection of general members of `|O(1,2)|` and `|O(2,2)|`. Both systems are very ample, so `C` is smooth by Bertini, of dimension 1. Its class is `(H_1+2H_2)(2H_1+2H_2) = 6H_1H_2 + 4H_2^2`, so `deg(pr_1|_C) = C \cdot H_1 = 4` and, by adjunction, `omega_C = (O(-2,-3) tensor O(1,2) tensor O(2,2))|_C = O(1,1)|_C` of degree `6+4 = 10`; hence `g(C) = 6`. Connectivity: the Koszul resolution `0 -> O(-3,-4) -> O(-1,-2)+O(-2,-2) -> I_C -> 0` together with the Kunneth vanishings `H^1(O(-1,-2)) = H^1(O(-2,-2)) = H^2(O(-3,-4)) = 0` gives `H^1(I_C) = 0`, so `h^0(O_C) = 1`. Pushing the Koszul resolution along `pr_1` (using `R^2 pr_{1*}O(-3,-4) = O(-3)^3` and the vanishing of `R^i pr_{1*}O(a,-2)`) gives `gamma_*O_C = O + O(-3)^3`, i.e. `E = O(3)^3` and `X = P(E^vee) = P^1 x P^2` with `O_X(1) = O(3,1)`. Then `O_X(2) tensor p^*O(-f) = O(6-f,2)`, so the two defining equations are sections of `W_5 = O(1,2)` and `W_4 = O(2,2)`, i.e. `F = O(4)+O(5)`: the cover is balanced. Consistently, `e_1 = 3` satisfies `2e_1 = 6 >= 4 = f_1`, and `L = omega_C(-D) = O(1,1)|_C tensor O(-1,0)|_C = O(0,1)|_C` has `h^0 = 3`, in agreement with Proposition 4.1.

This is a single existence verification; per the packet's execution boundary it establishes only the existence statement (the balanced locus is nonempty), and no universal claim is drawn from it.

---

## 10. Recorded constraints addressed, and what is not proved

- **`chi(L)=1` does not give a reduced member.** Not used that way; Lemma 5.1 proves it, using base-point-freeness or the single-base-point analysis plus a characteristic-zero genericity count - the mechanism the constraint itself names as required.
- **`P^2`-bundle over the whole balanced base without `h^0(D)=2`.** The hypothesis is *proved* (Proposition 3.1), so the conclusion is unconditional; and by Proposition 6.2 it holds over non-reduced bases too.
- **`Proj(pi_*L)` when `h^0` jumps.** `h^0` does not jump; base change is proved; and the Abel-Jacobi model of FND-0107 is used as the definition, with `P(pi_*L)` obtained as a theorem (Proposition 6.3), not by fiat.
- **Excess `= h^1(L) = 2` implies lci/smooth/pure/Tate.** Not used. Smoothness over `B` is proved directly; no purity, Gysin, Hodge or Tate statement is made anywhere.
- **Global splitting of `W` from fibrewise balancedness.** Not used; see Remark 6.1 and Proposition 7.3, which use the canonical filtration (CLM-0065-5) and only fibrewise splitting.
- **Constancy of `h^0(omega_C(-D))=3` identified with excluding all non-primitive pencils.** Explicitly not done; see Remark 3.4.
- **Reduced-support open called closed; non-closedness inferred.** Neither: it is called open, and no closedness or non-closedness of the balanced piece is claimed (no witness point is exhibited, as the constraint requires).
- **Ordering torsor on coarse moduli; reduction on one side only.** Stated at stack level on open subschemes, with no reduction applied at all.
- **Scheme-theoretic identification of the failure locus from fibrewise equivalence.** Not attempted here; imported from ATT-0065 (CLM-0065-4), which proves it at the level of Fitting ideals and is confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109.

**Not proved here:** anything about unbalanced splitting types; the non-reduced-support strata; closure, purity, or exhaustive component/stabilizer analysis of the evaluation-failure locus inside `M_{6,6}`; the value `b = 15` and its simple-branching hypothesis; density of the balanced locus in the tetragonal locus; and any weight, Hodge or Tate conclusion, in particular the exact target RED-0001, which this lemma does not address.

theorem_scope.not_covered: unbalanced CE splitting types; non-reduced-support strata and their scheme structure; closure of the balanced piece in M_{6,6} and any non-closedness witness; exhaustive component/stabilizer analysis of the full evaluation-failure locus in M_{6,6}; local complete intersection or depth statements for the determinantal presentation itself as opposed to the incidence scheme; any Gysin, localization, purity, weight, Hodge or Tate conclusion; the exact target RED-0001; the dimension count b=15 for the balanced tetragonal Hurwitz base and its simple-branching hypothesis; density of the balanced locus in the tetragonal locus

theorem_statement: Let k be a field of characteristic zero. (I) FIBREWISE PART. Let C be a smooth projective connected curve of genus 6 over an algebraically closed extension of k and let gamma:C->P^1 be a finite flat morphism of degree 4 with Casnati-Ekedahl data (E,F): gamma_*O_C = O + E^vee with E locally free of rank 3; X:=P(E^vee) with structure map p:X->P^1 normalized by p_*O_X(1)=E; i:C->X the CE embedding with gamma = p o i; and the degree-four CE ideal resolution 0 -> O_X(-4) tensor p^*det F -> O_X(-2) tensor p^*F -> I_C -> 0 with F locally free of rank two. Write E = O(e_1)+O(e_2)+O(e_3) with e_1<=e_2<=e_3 and F = O(f_1)+O(f_2) with f_1<=f_2, and put D:=gamma^*O_{P^1}(1), a base-point-free degree-four divisor class. Then: (1) deg E = sum e_i = 9, sum f_i = 9, deg(O_X(1)|_C)=18, O_X(1)|_C = omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2), and f_1 <= 2 e_1. (2) If (f_1,f_2)=(4,5) ('balanced'), then e_1>=2; consequently h^0(C,O_C(D))=2 exactly, gamma does not factor through any degree-two morphism C->P^1, and C is not hyperelliptic. (3) In the balanced case W_5:=(O_X(2) tensor p^*O(-5))|_C = omega_C^2(-D) and W_4:=(O_X(2) tensor p^*O(-4))|_C = omega_C^2, so L:=W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} = omega_C(-D) has deg L = 6, and h^0(L)=3 and h^1(L)=2 EXACTLY; moreover omega_C tensor L^{-1} = O_C(D), the linear system |omega_C tensor L^{-1}| is a base-point-free pencil, and gamma is recovered from the pair (C,L) up to Aut(P^1). (4) The complete linear system |L| = P(H^0(L)) is a plane P^2 inside Sym^6 C whose base locus is either empty or a single reduced point; the latter occurs only if C is a smooth plane quintic, in which case L = O_C(1)(q) and D ~ O_C(1)-q. In every balanced case the locus of divisors in |L| whose support consists of six pairwise distinct points is a NONEMPTY dense open subset of |L| with proper closed complement. (II) FAMILY PART. Let B be a locally Noetherian k-scheme, pi:C->B smooth and proper with geometrically connected genus-six fibres, s:P->B a P^1-bundle, and gamma:C->P a finite flat B-morphism of degree four whose CE data is balanced on every geometric fibre in the sense of (2). Choose any O_P(1) of relative degree one, put D:=gamma^*O_P(1) and L:=omega_{C/B}(-D); every statement below is invariant under L -> L tensor pi^*(invertible sheaf on B), so the Pic(B)-ambiguity of these choices is harmless, and no global splitting of F or of W is used. Then: (5) pi_*L and R^1pi_*L are locally free of ranks 3 and 2 and their formation commutes with arbitrary base change B'->B, with no reducedness hypothesis on B; the h^0-stratification of L over the balanced locus therefore consists of the single stratum h^0(L)=3. (6) The relative Abel-Jacobi incidence AJ := Sym^6(C/B) x_{Pic^6_{C/B},[L]} B, i.e. the closed subscheme of Sym^6(C/B) parametrizing relative effective degree-six divisors Gamma with O(Gamma) = L relatively, is canonically B-isomorphic to the projective bundle P(pi_*L); it is smooth and projective over B, Zariski-locally trivial with fibres P^2, of pure relative dimension exactly 2 over every point of B, and its closed immersion into the B-smooth Sym^6(C/B) is a regular immersion of codimension 4 -- whereas the generic determinantal expectation for the rank-drop ideal Fit_0(coker phi)=I_6(phi_5) of the corank-one 11-by-6 evaluation is codimension 6. (7) The reduced-support open AJ^{rs} of AJ meets every geometric fibre of AJ->B in a dense open subset; hence AJ^{rs}->B is smooth and surjective with geometrically irreducible two-dimensional fibres and AJ^{rs} is dense open in AJ. The ordered incidence Z := Conf_6(C/B) x_{Sym^6(C/B)} AJ is a finite etale S_6-torsor over AJ^{rs} (at stack level, on open subschemes, with no reduction applied to either side) and is smooth over B of pure relative dimension 2; and by ATT-0065 (CLM-0065-1,3,4,5, confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109), applied over the base Conf_6(C/B) with its six tautological pairwise-disjoint sections, Z is exactly the intrinsic Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure scheme V(Fit_0(coker phi)) = a_N^{-1}(e) there. In particular the balanced evaluation-failure scheme has no fibre of dimension different from 2 and no component of relative dimension greater than 2 over any point of B, special or general. (8) If moreover B is of finite type over k of pure dimension b, then Z is of pure dimension b+2 and every irreducible component of Z dominates a component of B. If in addition B is a moduli stack of balanced tetragonal covers (objects the pairs (C/T,gamma), isomorphisms the isomorphisms of such pairs), then the classifying morphism c:Z->M_{6,6}, (b;p_1,...,p_6) |-> (C_b;p_1,...,p_6), is a monomorphism: it is injective on isomorphism classes of T-points and induces isomorphisms on automorphism groups; consequently c has zero-dimensional geometric fibres and the image of c has dimension b+2, which equals 17, i.e. codimension 4 in the 21-dimensional M_{6,6}, whenever b=15. No closedness, purity, component-exhaustion, Gysin, Hodge, weight or Tate assertion is made anywhere in this theorem, and nothing is asserted for unbalanced CE splitting types.
